options.name: transcription_model

options.name: use_azure
options.effect: Selects Azure OpenAI (AZURE_API_KEY / AZURE_ENDPOINT / AZURE_DEPLOYMENT) vs standard OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY) -- but ONLY when api_config is not supplied. The card's construct line passes api_config=get_openai_config(use_azure=...) explicitly, and an explicit api_config wins outright, so set the provider in one place: either build the config yourself or pass this flag, not both.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.provider -- must match every other component in the blueprint; a mixed-provider blueprint fails on whichever component lacks the credentials

options.name: model
options.effect: Model / Azure deployment used for both enhancement passes. None uses the deployment named in the config. CONSTRAINT: this component hardcodes temperature=0 on every call and exposes no override, so models above gpt-5.4 (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-sol, ...) -- which have no temperature parameter at all -- fail here with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model". There is no kwarg workaround: choose gpt-5.4 or a conventional model (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, ...).
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model, subject to the constraint above -- if the blueprint targets a model above gpt-5.4, this component must run on a different model or be dropped

options.name: reasoning_effort
options.effect: Reasoning effort for the enhancement calls ('none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' -- gaik's GPT-model vocabulary; there is no 'max' tier). None omits it, which is what non-reasoning models require. Higher effort helps on garbled ASR output and heavy domain jargon, at the cost of latency on every chunk. On gpt-5.4, leave this omitted/None: the component always sends temperature=0.0, and gpt-5.4 accepts that temperature only when reasoning_effort is omitted or set to Python None. Setting an ACTIVE effort (low/medium/high) here makes the call fail, since there is no kwarg to drop the hardcoded temperature in compensation.
options.infer_from: transcript quality is poor or the domain vocabulary is specialised -> 'low'/'medium' on a reasoning model that is not gpt-5.4; otherwise leave null

schema, requirements = _load_output_schema(schema_dir)
    if schema is None:
        schema = schema_gen.generate_schema(user_requirements=user_requirements)

SchemaGenerator.note: Use _load_output_schema() first -- the wizard pre-generates the schema; only call generate_schema() when _load_output_schema() returns None. Schema files are always named output_schema.* regardless of the class name.

options.name: temperature
options.effect: Sampling temperature for schema generation. The 0.0 default makes the same requirements yield the same schema and is correct for conventional models (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, ...). MODEL RULES: (a) gpt-5.4 accepts an explicit temperature only when reasoning_effort is omitted or set to Python None. When reasoning_effort is low, medium, or high, set temperature=None so the temperature parameter is omitted from the API request. (b) Models after gpt-5.4, such as gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6-sol, do not support an explicit temperature -- set temperature=None for these models, regardless of reasoning effort. In both cases, temperature=None drops the parameter from the request entirely (gaik never sends null; _sampling_kwargs builds the request by inclusion). Leaving the kwarg off entirely is NOT the same as passing None: the default 0.0 IS still sent, and fails with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model."
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model above gpt-5.4 (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-sol, ...) -> temperature=None. gpt-5.4 with no reasoning_effort -> leave 0.0 so the same requirements yield the same schema; gpt-5.4 with reasoning_effort low/medium/high -> temperature=None. Conventional models -> leave 0.0.

options.name: reasoning_effort
options.effect: Reasoning effort for schema generation ('none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' -- gaik's GPT-model vocabulary; there is no 'max' tier). None omits the parameter from the request entirely. What the underlying model does when reasoning_effort is absent is not documented by gaik and has not been independently verified here -- do not assume omission behaves like an explicit 'no reasoning' setting. Higher effort helps when the requirements describe nested or conditional structures, at the cost of latency. On gpt-5.4, setting an ACTIVE effort (low/medium/high) here requires pairing it with temperature=None (see temperature); leaving this parameter omitted/None is what pairs with an explicit temperature -- there is no supported combination of an active effort with an explicit temperature.
options.infer_from: target_output_spec has nested objects, conditional fields, or many interdependent fields -> 'medium'/'high'; flat field lists -> leave null (the model's own behavior when omitted is unverified -- do not assume it means 'no reasoning'). Pair with the temperature rule for the chosen model.

options.name: model
options.effect: Model / Azure deployment for schema generation. None uses the deployment in the config dict. Schema generation runs once per pipeline, so it can afford a stronger model than the per-document extraction step.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model; a complex nested target schema justifies a stronger model here than for extraction. Note there is no use_azure kwarg on this component -- the provider is fixed by whatever built the config dict passed to config=.

options.name: save_json
options.effect: When True, writes the list of extracted result dicts to a JSON file at json_path after extraction completes.
options.infer_from: integration_targets include file export or audit trail -> set True and configure json_path; otherwise leave False

options.name: temperature
options.effect: Sampling temperature. The 0.0 default gives deterministic extraction and is correct for conventional models (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, ...). MODEL RULES: (a) gpt-5.4 accepts an explicit temperature only when reasoning_effort is omitted or set to Python None. When reasoning_effort is low, medium, or high, set temperature=None so the temperature parameter is omitted from the API request. (b) Models after gpt-5.4, such as gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6-sol, do not support an explicit temperature -- set temperature=None for these models, regardless of reasoning effort. In both cases, temperature=None drops the parameter from the request entirely (gaik never sends null; _sampling_kwargs builds the request by inclusion). Leaving the kwarg off entirely is NOT the same as passing None: the default 0.0 IS still sent, and fails with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported."
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model above gpt-5.4 (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-sol, ...) -> temperature=None. gpt-5.4 with no reasoning_effort -> leave 0.0 for deterministic extraction; gpt-5.4 with reasoning_effort low/medium/high -> temperature=None. Conventional models -> leave 0.0.

options.name: reasoning_effort
options.effect: Reasoning effort for the extraction call ('none' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' -- gaik's GPT-model vocabulary; there is no 'max' tier). None omits the parameter from the request entirely. What the underlying model does when reasoning_effort is absent is not documented by gaik and has not been independently verified here -- do not assume omission behaves like an explicit 'no reasoning' setting. Raising it helps on ambiguous or sparsely-stated source text at the cost of latency. On gpt-5.4, setting an ACTIVE effort (low/medium/high) here requires pairing it with temperature=None (see temperature); leaving this parameter omitted/None is what pairs with an explicit temperature -- there is no supported combination of an active effort with an explicit temperature.
options.infer_from: source documents are ambiguous, inconsistent, or require inference across sections -> 'medium'/'high'; straightforward forms -> leave null (the model's own behavior when omitted is unverified -- do not assume it means 'no reasoning'). Pair with the temperature rule for the chosen model.

options.name: model
options.effect: Model / Azure deployment for extraction. None uses the deployment in the config dict. This is the per-document cost driver: it runs once per input, unlike schema generation which runs once per pipeline.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model. No use_azure kwarg exists here -- the provider is fixed by the config dict. Inside DocumentsToStructuredData / AudioToStructuredData, 'model' is the ONLY extractor_ctor key that also reaches the internal SchemaGenerator; every other key goes to DataExtractor alone.

(LLMJudge names the same vendor 'anthropic', so the two components are not interchangeable.) Pair with use_azure for openai/claude, or vertex_ai for google.

options.name: additional_instructions
options.effect: Extra text appended to the user extraction prompt. Use to inject domain-specific rules, field-level hints, or language directives without replacing the built-in prompt.
options.infer_from: domain_vocabulary OR special extraction rules exist -> encode as additional_instructions; leave null for standard extraction

options.name: use_azure
options.effect: Azure OpenAI vs standard OpenAI. Applies ONLY when model_provider is 'openai' or 'claude' (it is forwarded to get_openai_config / get_claude_config); it is ignored entirely when model_provider='google' -- use vertex_ai for that path -- and when api_config is supplied.

options.name: model
options.effect: Model / deployment override for the selected model_provider. None uses whatever the provider config names. The valid values differ per provider, so this must be set together with model_provider, never independently.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model, paired with the matching model_provider

options.name: reasoning_effort
options.effect: DIFFERENT vocabulary from the extractor components (SchemaGenerator/DataExtractor/TranscriptEnhancer, which accept 'none'|'low'|'medium'|'high'): VisionExtractor accepts only 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' -- 'none' is NOT accepted here, so reasoning cannot be turned off, only turned down. It also DEFAULTS to 'medium' rather than off, so VisionExtractor always spends reasoning tokens unless you lower it; this is a standing cost item on high-volume page-by-page extraction. On the google/Vertex path it is sent as generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel and upper-cased automatically.

options.name: vertex_ai

This changes which credentials the PoC needs, so it must be decided before the env template is written.

VisionParser.call_page_citations:
pages = parser.convert_pdf(str(input_path), clean_output=False)
    # DO NOT join -- each list index is one page, needed for file_name|page_number citations
    file_name = input_path.name
    cited_pages = [(file_name, page_num, page_text) for page_num, page_text in enumerate(pages, start=1)]
VisionParser.returns: list[str] (markdown pages). With clean_output=True and >1 page, this is a ONE-ELEMENT list containing the merged/cleaned markdown for the whole document -- NOT one element per page. Page-level attribution requires clean_output=False.

options.name: custom_prompt
options.effect: Overrides the built-in page-conversion prompt. When set, the supplied text replaces the default 'Convert this document page to accurate markdown' instruction sent to the vision model.
options.infer_from: domain_vocabulary OR special formatting requirements -> ask for a custom extraction prompt

options.name: use_context
options.effect: When True, feeds the LAST 500 CHARACTERS of the previous page's markdown to the model so that tables and sections that span page boundaries are continued seamlessly. TRADEOFF when citations are required: this lets the model's output for page N be influenced by page N-1's content, which weakens strict claims that a given statement came ONLY from page N. When exact page attribution matters more than cross-page table continuity, set use_context=False.
options.infer_from: multi-page documents with cross-page tables AND page-exact citation is not required -> leave True (default). Citations must identify exactly where each statement appeared -> False, even at the cost of split-table continuity.

options.name: dpi
options.effect: PDF-to-image rendering resolution passed to PyMuPDF. Higher DPI improves OCR quality on dense or small-font pages at the cost of larger images and higher token usage.
options.infer_from: inputs are low-DPI scans OR small-font dense documents -> suggest raising to 300

options.name: clean_output
options.effect: DECIDES WHETHER PAGE CITATIONS ARE POSSIBLE AT ALL. When True and the PDF has more than one page, runs a second LLM call that merges ALL pages into a SINGLE list element (return value collapses from N pages to 1) -- this is NOT a formatting pass, it destroys page-level attribution. When False, convert_pdf() returns one list element per page, page number = index + 1. The card's own default 'call' example uses clean_output=True and joins the result -- do NOT copy that pattern when the use case needs file_name|page_number citations; use 'call_page_citations' instead.
options.infer_from: page-level citations required (file_name|page_number) -> False, and keep pages as a list, do not join. Single-page documents, or multi-page with no citation requirement -> True is fine (or moot for single-page input).

options.name: max_tokens
options.effect: Caps output tokens (max_completion_tokens) on every page-conversion and cleanup call. Dense pages with heavy tables can be truncated mid-page if this is too low, silently dropping the tail of the page.
options.infer_from: pages are dense/text-heavy or table-rich -> raise (e.g. 24000-32000); short simple pages -> default is fine

options.name: temperature
options.effect: Sampling temperature, sent unconditionally on every call (type is float, not float | None -- there is no way to omit it through this constructor). VisionParser has no reasoning_effort parameter at all, so on gpt-5.4 the default 0.0 works (gpt-5.4 accepts a custom temperature only while no reasoning_effort is active, and this component never sends one). On models ABOVE gpt-5.4 (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-sol, ...), which have no temperature parameter at all, this component has NO working configuration -- the value is always forwarded literally and fails with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model". There is no kwarg workaround; use a different parser or a different model for vision conversion above gpt-5.4.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.model above gpt-5.4 -> this component cannot be used, pick MultimodalParser or another vision path instead; gpt-5.4 or conventional models -> leave 0.0 for deterministic markdown conversion

PyMuPDFParser.call_page_citations:
res = parser.parse_document(str(input_path), use_markdown=False)
    # text_content now contains '=== PAGE N ===' markers -- split on them to recover per-page text
    import re
    file_name = input_path.name
    raw_pages = re.split(r'=== PAGE (\d+) ===', res['text_content'])[1:]
    cited_pages = [(file_name, int(raw_pages[i]), raw_pages[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(raw_pages), 2)]
PyMuPDFParser.returns: dict(.text_content, .word_count, .content_length). With use_markdown=True (default), .text_content is one flat string, pages concatenated with no marker -- no page-level provenance. With use_markdown=False, .text_content contains '=== PAGE N ===' markers per page plus per-line [x:,y:] bounding-box tags -- this is the only way this parser supports file_name|page_number citations, and it is opt-in, not the default.

options.name: use_markdown
options.effect: DECIDES WHETHER PAGE CITATIONS ARE POSSIBLE. When True (default), extracts plain text concatenated page by page with NO page marker -- page provenance cannot be recovered. When False, inserts explicit '=== PAGE N ===' markers into text_content (see _extract_structured_pdf) AND annotates every text span with (x, y) bounding-box coordinates. This is the cheapest way to get file_name|page_number citations for a text-layer PDF -- free and local, unlike VisionParser -- but the bounding-box tags add real noise to the text that an extraction prompt must tolerate or a preprocessing step must strip. Has no OCR either way: on scanned/image-only PDFs, text_content may come back empty or incomplete regardless of this setting -- check content_length/word_count rather than assuming success means real content.
options.infer_from: page-level citations required on a text-layer (non-scanned) PDF -> False, using call_page_citations; downstream needs positional/layout data -> False; otherwise leave True (default, cleanest plain text)

DocxParser.returns: dict(.text_content). No page-level provenance -- .docx is a reflowable format with no fixed page model, so file_name|page_number citations cannot be recovered by any means.

options.name: use_markdown
options.effect: When True, extracts plain paragraph and table text. When False, emits a structured representation with paragraph-index, style-name, and table-cell markers - useful for style-aware downstream processing, but still has no page numbers to offer.
options.infer_from: downstream needs paragraph style / formatting metadata -> False; otherwise leave True

options.name: hybrid_search
options.effect: Combine semantic + keyword search.
options.infer_from: queries mix exact terms (codes, names, IDs) with conceptual questions

options.name: re_rank
options.effect: Cross-encoder re-ranking of retrieved results.
options.infer_from: retrieval precision is critical

options.name: top_k
options.effect: Number of chunks retrieved.
options.infer_from: answer breadth requirement

options.name: score_threshold
options.effect: Drops any chunk scoring below the threshold, so search() can return FEWER than top_k results (or none at all). This is the precision/recall lever: raise it to suppress weak, off-topic context that would otherwise pad the prompt and invite hallucination; leave it null when recall matters more than precision. CRITICAL -- the threshold is applied AFTER hybrid scoring and re-ranking, so the score scale it compares against changes with the other options: plain semantic search yields cosine similarity (~0..1), hybrid_search yields 0.7*vector + 0.3*BM25, and re_rank yields raw cross-encoder logits which are unbounded and frequently NEGATIVE. A value tuned for one mode will silently discard everything (or nothing) in another -- retune whenever hybrid_search or re_rank changes.
options.infer_from: answer must be grounded / 'do not answer if the documents do not cover it' / precision-critical domains (legal, medical, compliance) -> set a threshold and tune it against the chosen scoring mode; exploratory or broad-recall search -> leave null

options.name: filters
options.effect: Search-time metadata scoping (a search() argument, not a constructor argument). Restricts retrieval to chunks whose Document.metadata matches -- exact equality per key, ANDed across keys; there are no operators, ranges, or OR. Only works if the ingestion step actually wrote those metadata keys. This is how you get per-tenant, per-document, per-department or per-date-bucket isolation out of a single shared collection instead of provisioning one store per scope.
options.infer_from: multi-tenant or per-user data isolation, 'only search within this document/case/department', or any access-control requirement -> plan the metadata keys at ingestion and pass filters at search time

options.name: include_scores
options.effect: A search() argument. Writes the final relevance score onto each returned chunk as Document.metadata['relevance_score']. It does NOT change the return type -- the call still returns list[Document]. Needed whenever the UI shows confidence, or the app applies its own post-filtering or sorting; without it the scores are computed and then thrown away.
options.infer_from: UI displays confidence/relevance, or the app post-filters retrieved chunks -> true; plain answer generation -> false

options.name: rerank_model
options.effect: Cross-encoder used when re_rank=True; ignored otherwise. Loaded via sentence-transformers, so the first call downloads the weights and it runs locally on CPU/GPU rather than via the API. The default is English-trained -- on Finnish or other non-English corpora, either swap in a multilingual cross-encoder or leave re_rank off, since an English-only re-ranker can score worse than no re-ranking at all.
options.infer_from: re_rank is true AND the corpus language is not English -> pick a multilingual cross-encoder; offline/air-gapped deployment -> note the model download requirement

Retriever.note: top_k, hybrid_search, re_rank and score_threshold can each be set on the constructor as a default and then overridden per call in search(), so one Retriever can serve both a broad-recall and a precision-first query path. filters and include_scores are search()-only.

options.name: stream

options.name: prompt

options.name: conversation_history
options.effect: Turns single-shot Q&A into a multi-turn chat: prior question/answer pairs are prepended to the messages so follow-ups like 'and what about last year?' resolve. Constructing a fresh one per request (the usual pattern in a stateless web handler) silently resets the memory and the flag does nothing. Note the retriever is not history-aware: follow-up queries are still embedded verbatim, so pronoun-only follow-ups may retrieve poor context even when the generator understands them.

options.name: last_n
options.effect: How many prior Q/A PAIRS are kept and replayed when conversation_history=True -- 10 pairs is 20 messages, and every one is re-sent on each turn, so this is a direct cost and context-window lever on long sessions. Ignored when conversation_history=False.
options.infer_from: long chat sessions or a tight token budget -> lower it (3-5); short sessions needing full recall -> leave 10

The 0.0 default is deliberate -- the same question should yield the same SQL -- and is correct for conventional models (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, ...). This component has no reasoning_effort kwarg, but if the deployment itself runs with active reasoning (e.g. an Azure deployment configured for it), MODEL RULES: (a) gpt-5.4 accepts an explicit temperature only when the deployment's effective reasoning_effort is omitted or Python None; under active reasoning, gaik's own guidance elsewhere is to set temperature=None -- there is no exposed reasoning_effort here to pair it with, so if reproducible SQL fails under active reasoning, that is a sign this component is unsuitable for that deployment. (b) Models after gpt-5.4, such as gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6-sol, do not support an explicit temperature -- set temperature=None for these models, regardless of reasoning effort. In both cases, temperature=None drops the parameter from the request entirely (sending null is not the same as not sending it). Leaving the kwarg off entirely is NOT the same as passing None: the default 0.0 IS still sent, and fails with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model".

Do NOT also add Transcriber / TranscriptEnhancer / SchemaGenerator / DataExtractor as separate steps. LIMITATION: it drives Transcriber on the hosted path, so the transcript it extracts from carries no timestamps and no speaker labels. If the use case needs either -- time-coded citations, subtitles, who-said-what -- do not use this module; decompose into an explicit transcription step (see the provenance override in SKILL.md Phase 5) + SchemaGenerator + DataExtractor. MODELS ABOVE gpt-5.4 (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-sol, ...): these have no temperature parameter, but the module constructs SchemaGenerator itself with the default temperature=0.0 and no kwarg reaches it (extractor_ctor forwards only to DataExtractor), so schema generation fails with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model". Work around it by pre-generating the schema and passing schema= + requirements= (which skips SchemaGenerator entirely), or decompose into explicit SchemaGenerator + DataExtractor steps where temperature=None can be set. On gpt-5.4 the module works as-is: SchemaGenerator sends no reasoning_effort by default, and gpt-5.4 accepts a temperature while no effort is set.

Do NOT also add a parser / SchemaGenerator / DataExtractor as separate steps; choose the internal parser via parser_choice and configure it via parser_ctor. MODELS ABOVE gpt-5.4 (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.6-sol, ...): these have no temperature parameter, but the module constructs SchemaGenerator itself with the default temperature=0.0 and no kwarg reaches it (extractor_ctor forwards only to DataExtractor), so schema generation fails with "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0 with this model". Work around it by pre-generating the schema and passing schema= + requirements= (which skips SchemaGenerator entirely), or decompose into explicit SchemaGenerator + DataExtractor steps where temperature=None can be set. On gpt-5.4 the module works as-is: SchemaGenerator sends no reasoning_effort by default, and gpt-5.4 accepts a temperature while no effort is set.

RAGWorkflow.construct: workflow = RAGWorkflow(use_azure=use_azure, persist=True, persist_path=str(output_dir / 'chroma_store'), citations=True, stream=False)

options.name: citations
options.effect: Include source citations in the answer. ON by default -- unlike the standalone AnswerGenerator, where citations defaults to false.
options.infer_from: leave true unless the requirements explicitly say citations are undesired in the output

options.name: retriever_top_k
options.effect: Number of chunks retrieved.
options.infer_from: answer breadth requirement

options.name: retriever_hybrid
options.effect: Enables hybrid BM25 + vector search in the Retriever. Improves recall when queries mix exact terms (codes, IDs, names) with conceptual questions.
options.infer_from: queries mix exact keyword terms (product codes, names, IDs) with conceptual or semantic questions

options.name: retriever_rerank
options.effect: Enables cross-encoder re-ranking of retrieved chunks for higher retrieval precision. Adds one extra inference pass per query.
options.infer_from: retrieval precision is critical OR accuracy_critical == yes

options.name: conversation_history
options.effect: Maintains the last `last_n` Q/A pairs as context for subsequent questions. Enables follow-up questions but increases prompt size.
options.infer_from: multi-turn chat / conversational interface required; set false for single-shot batch Q&A

options.name: stream
options.effect: Stream answer tokens from the AnswerGenerator instead of waiting for the full response.
options.infer_from: runtime_interface: interactive/chat UI -> true; batch pipeline or API -> false

options.name: last_n
options.effect: Number of Q/A pairs retained in conversation history when conversation_history=True.
options.infer_from: conversation_history == true; leave default unless the user specifies a context window budget

options.name: retriever_threshold
options.effect: Minimum similarity score for a chunk to be included in results. Filters out low-relevance chunks; None means no threshold.
options.infer_from: technical tuning; leave None unless retrieval returns too many low-relevance results

options.name: persist
options.effect: When true, uses a persistent Chroma vector store at persist_path. When false, the store is in-memory only and lost after the process exits.
options.infer_from: always true for production use; set false only for ephemeral tests or demos

options.name: use_azure
options.effect: Azure OpenAI vs standard OpenAI. Used to build api_config when none is supplied, and it then governs BOTH the embedder and the answer generator inside the workflow -- there is no way to split providers between them from here.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.provider -- must match the credentials in the PoC env template

options.name: embedding_model
options.effect: Embedding model / deployment for ingestion and query embedding. None uses the config default. CRITICAL with persist=True: the embedding model determines the vector dimension (text-embedding-3-small = 1536, text-embedding-3-large = 3072), and it is baked into the persisted collection at persist_path. Changing it later against an existing store either errors on a dimension mismatch or, worse, silently mixes incompatible vectors and returns nonsense -- delete the store and re-ingest when you change this.
options.infer_from: corpus size and retrieval quality needs; if the blueprint also configures a PgVectorStore or Embedder elsewhere, this MUST name the same embedding model, and embedding_dim must match it

options.name: persist_path
options.effect: Directory for the persistent Chroma store when persist=True. Relative paths resolve against the process working directory, not the PoC's own location -- in generated code, pass an absolute path (e.g. str(output_dir / 'chroma_store')) so re-running the script from a different working directory does not silently create or read a different store. Ignored when persist=False.
options.infer_from: always set explicitly to an absolute path in generated PoC code; leave the bare default only for quick ad-hoc scripts

options.name: collection_name
options.effect: Chroma collection name. Multiple RAGWorkflow instances sharing the same persist_path but different collection_name values keep separate indexes in the same store directory -- useful for multi-tenant or multi-corpus setups without provisioning separate persist paths. Changing it against an existing persist_path starts a fresh, empty collection rather than erroring.
options.infer_from: multiple distinct document sets share one persist_path -> give each a distinct collection_name; single-corpus use -> leave default

RAGWorkflow.note: End-to-end module: embeds, stores, retrieves, and answers. Do NOT also add Embedder / PgVectorStore / Retriever / AnswerGenerator as separate steps.

ParallelTranscriber.import:
from gaik.software_components.parallel_transcriber import ParallelTranscriber, TranscriptionConfig
    from gaik.software_components.config import get_openai_config

options.name: response_format
options.effect: Output format; 'srt'/'vtt' give timestamped subtitles, 'text' plain transcript. This is the cloud path to timestamps -- no self-hosted endpoint needed, unlike Transcriber(whisper_local). CAUTION: 'json' and 'verbose_json' are accepted but NOT specially handled -- _convert_format() returns the raw SRT text unchanged for both, so neither one yields the structured segment/word objects the name implies. Use 'srt' and parse it yourself if structured timing data is needed.
options.infer_from: output_types: subtitles/captions -> srt or vtt; any requirement for timestamps or citations that locate a claim in the audio -> srt; plain transcript -> text

options.name: model
options.effect: Transcription backend. All three yield timestamps. NONE of them yields speaker labels to the caller: GPT4O_DIARIZE requests diarized_json and parses the speaker field, then drops it when building the SRT (_segments_to_srt is called without include_speaker=True), and TranscriptionResult exposes only .content, so there is no way to recover it; WHISPER_LOCAL hardcodes diarization=False in its request payload. WHISPER_LOCAL also needs api_config['api_base'] (required) and api_config['key'] (optional), not the cloud provider config.
options.infer_from: leave at WHISPER unless technical_spec.model says otherwise. Do NOT select GPT4O_DIARIZE to satisfy a speaker-attribution requirement -- it does not deliver one; use Transcriber(transcription_model='whisper_local', diarization=True) instead.

options.name: chunk_duration_minutes
options.effect: Nominal chunk length for parallel splitting.
options.infer_from: leave default unless the user tunes throughput

options.name: language
options.effect: ISO 639-1 language code passed to Whisper (e.g., 'fi', 'en'). None means auto-detect. Setting explicitly improves accuracy when the language is known.
options.infer_from: technical_spec.language - set when source language is known and not mixed

options.name: prompt
options.effect: Optional Whisper prompt to bias the decoder toward domain vocabulary or proper nouns.
options.infer_from: domain_vocabulary is present - provide key terms to reduce ASR errors

options.name: transcription_workers
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Number of chunks transcribed concurrently -- but ONLY for the default WHISPER model. GPT4O_DIARIZE uses its own gpt4o_chunk_parallelism (default 4) and WHISPER_LOCAL uses whisper_local_chunk_parallelism (default 2); setting transcription_workers has no effect on either. Set the field matching whichever model option is chosen.
options.infer_from: model == WHISPER (default) AND high volume / throughput matters -> raise; watch for rate limits on the transcription API

options.name: max_single_file_mb
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Files at or below this size skip chunking entirely and transcribe in a single pass -- no splitting, no parallelism, lowest overhead. Above it, the file is split into chunk_duration_minutes-long pieces and processed in parallel. For GPT4O_DIARIZE this is combined with a hard 25-minute duration cap that forces chunking regardless of file size.
options.infer_from: typical input file size relative to 24MB -- lower it to force chunking/parallelism sooner on a fast network; raise it to avoid chunking overhead on slightly larger single-pass-capable files

options.name: chunk_overlap_seconds
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Seconds of audio duplicated between adjacent chunk boundaries so a word or sentence spoken across a cut is not lost. Larger overlap improves boundary accuracy at the cost of slightly more audio processed (and, for GPT4O_DIARIZE, more tokens billed) per chunk.
options.infer_from: leave default unless boundary-accuracy issues are observed (raise) or cost is tight and chunks are long (lower)

options.name: max_retries
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Retry attempts for transient (5xx) failures per chunk, with retry_base_delay_seconds (default 1.0s) as the backoff base. Separate from max_429_retries (default 4), which governs rate-limit backoff specifically and is not capped by this value -- total_max_attempts = max_retries + 1 + max_429_retries.
options.infer_from: unreliable network or a provider with frequent transient errors -> raise; leave default otherwise

options.name: gpt4o_chunk_parallelism
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Parallel chunk workers used ONLY when model=GPT4O_DIARIZE; paired with gpt4o_chunk_duration_minutes (default 23, just under the API's 25-minute limit). Ignored for every other model.
options.infer_from: model == GPT4O_DIARIZE AND throughput/cost tuning is needed

options.name: whisper_local_chunk_parallelism
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Parallel chunk workers used ONLY when model=WHISPER_LOCAL; kept low by default since this hits a single self-hosted GPU endpoint rather than a scaled cloud API -- raising it can just queue requests behind the same GPU instead of adding real throughput.
options.infer_from: model == WHISPER_LOCAL AND the self-hosted endpoint has spare GPU capacity to parallelize across

options.name: gpt4o_chunk_duration_minutes
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Nominal chunk length used ONLY when model=GPT4O_DIARIZE, paired with gpt4o_chunk_parallelism. Kept just under the API's 25-minute hard limit for that model -- raising it toward or past 25 causes chunk-level transcription failures. Ignored for every other model.
options.infer_from: model == GPT4O_DIARIZE; leave default -- it is already tuned to the API's own duration ceiling

options.name: whisper_local_chunk_duration_minutes
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Nominal chunk length used ONLY when model=WHISPER_LOCAL, paired with whisper_local_chunk_parallelism. Chunking only triggers once total duration exceeds this value; also bounded on the low end by whisper_local_request_timeout_seconds (default 1800s) -- a chunk that takes longer than that to process on the self-hosted endpoint times out. Ignored for every other model.
options.infer_from: model == WHISPER_LOCAL AND the self-hosted endpoint is slower or faster than typical -> adjust so a single chunk reliably finishes within the request timeout

options.name: whisper_local_max_audio_minutes
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. HARD CAP used ONLY when model=WHISPER_LOCAL -- audio longer than this raises ValueError('Audio too long for whisper_local ...') immediately, before any transcription is attempted. This is a fail-fast guard, not a degrade-gracefully limit: there is no automatic fallback to the cloud path. If the use case has audio that can exceed 6 hours, either raise this explicitly or route long files to a different model.
options.infer_from: model == WHISPER_LOCAL AND typical/maximum input audio length -> raise if recordings can exceed 6 hours; otherwise leave default and treat as a validation guard

options.name: max_429_retries
options.effect: TranscriptionConfig field. Retry attempts specifically for HTTP 429 (rate-limit) responses. The delay honors the server's Retry-After header when present, falling back to retry_base_delay_seconds * 1.5 * 2^attempt otherwise -- separate from and additional to max_retries, which covers transient 5xx failures. total_max_attempts = max_retries + 1 + max_429_retries.
options.infer_from: transcription provider has tight rate limits or large batch jobs trigger frequent 429s -> raise; leave default otherwise

ParallelTranscriber.note: FFmpeg + ffprobe must be on PATH. Use this instead of Transcriber for long media or when fast parallel throughput matters; it does not do Finnish enhancement (no enhanced_transcript option).

MultiSourceReportGenerator.call:
result = generator.run(
    input_paths=input_paths,
    sections=[
        {"id": "findings", "title": "Findings", "instructions": "Describe key findings from the evidence."},
        {"id": "recommendations", "title": "Recommendations", "instructions": "Give recommendations.", "depends_on": ["findings"]}
    ],
    report_title=report_title,
    report_description=report_description,
    report_language=report_language,
    sample_report_path=sample_report_path,
    output_dir=output_dir,
    output_docx=False,
    agentic=True,
    curate_evidence=False,
    polish=False,
    writer_options={"model": "gpt-5.4"}
)
    report_markdown = result.markdown
    written_sections = [s.title for s in result.sections]
    docx_path = result.docx_path

options.name: agentic
options.effect: When true, each section is drafted independently, fact-checked, and repaired by a diff-editor reviewer before the report is assembled. Higher accuracy; more API calls. Requires the multi-source-report-generator-agentic extra (langgraph).
options.infer_from: accuracy_critical == yes OR multi_section_hierarchical_report OR formal_client_facing_report

options.name: report_description
options.effect: Short description of the report's purpose and audience; passed as shared context to the writer, reviewer, and polish pass to keep tone and focus consistent.
options.infer_from: report purpose or audience is known from requirements

options.name: parser_choice
options.effect: Which PDF parser the module uses internally to normalize documents.
options.infer_from: input_formats: text PDF -> auto/pymupdf; scanned/visual PDF -> vision/docling

options.name: sample_report_path
options.effect: Path to a sample report whose structure, style, and tone the output should follow. Content is still drawn only from the evidence. In agentic mode the sample is split by ## headings and matched per section.
options.infer_from: user supplies an example or target report format

options.name: report_language
options.effect: Language to write the report in (e.g. 'English', 'Finnish').
options.infer_from: technical_spec.language

options.name: curate_evidence
options.effect: Agentic mode only. When true, a per-section LLM call extracts a focused evidence brief before drafting, improving relevance for reports with large evidence packs.
options.infer_from: agentic == true AND (large_evidence_pack OR many_sections)

options.name: polish
options.effect: Agentic mode only. Runs a final style and proofreading pass after the mandatory reviewer repair.
options.infer_from: agentic == true AND high_quality_output_required

options.name: output_docx
options.effect: Also write report.docx alongside report.md. Requires the multi-source-report-generator-docx extra and the Pandoc system binary.
options.infer_from: output_format == word OR user requests .docx

options.name: strict_review
options.effect: Agentic mode only. When true, raises before writing any output if the diff-editor reviewer has unresolved edits after retries. Use when the report must never be persisted with unresolved reviewer corrections.
options.infer_from: agentic == true AND (human_review == yes OR accuracy_critical)

options.name: review_options
options.effect: Agentic mode only. LLM config dict for the reviewer pass (same shape as writer_options). When None, the reviewer reuses the writer model/config.
options.infer_from: user specifies a separate or stronger model for fact-checking

options.name: include_source_references
options.effect: When true, the writer cites source filenames inline. Automatically suppressed when only one input source is provided.
options.infer_from: citation or traceability requirement; set false when citations are undesirable in the output

options.name: section_context_mode
options.effect: Controls what evidence context each section writer receives. Currently only all_evidence is supported.
options.infer_from: reserved for future use

options.name: verbose
options.effect: When true, prints per-section progress messages to the console during an agentic run: evidence loading, optional curation, drafting, reviewer corrections applied, and polish pass. Has no effect in single-call mode.
options.infer_from: agentic == true -> always set true in PoC so the user can see the per-section workflow at the CLI

options.name: writer_options
options.effect: LLM config dict for the report writer. Key: 'model' (e.g. 'gpt-5.4'). When None, the module uses its default model. Passed to every section-writing LLM call in both single-call and agentic mode.
options.infer_from: user specifies a writing/extraction model -> set writer_options={'model': '<model>'}

options.name: transcriber_options
options.effect: Options passed to the internal Transcriber when audio/video files are among the inputs. Common keys: 'model' (transcription model, e.g. 'gpt-4o-transcribe'), 'language' (ISO 639-1, e.g. 'fi'), 'enhanced_transcript' (bool, Finnish two-pass enhancement). When None, the Transcriber uses its own defaults.
options.infer_from: input contains audio/video -> always set; model: 'gpt-4o-transcribe' for standard use; language: infer from technical_spec.language; enhanced_transcript: true for Finnish audio

options.name: report_title
options.effect: Title placed at the top of the generated report and DOCX file.
options.infer_from: report type and customer name are known -> set a descriptive title (e.g. 'AI Consultancy Report')

options.name: include_evidence_index
options.effect: When true, writes an evidence_index.json alongside the report listing every source file processed. Useful for audit trails; set false to suppress.
options.infer_from: audit trail or source-traceability requirement -> leave true; suppress only if explicitly unwanted

options.name: max_evidence_chars
options.effect: Hard cap on the total character length of the assembled evidence pack passed to the writer. Prevents context-window overflows for very large source sets. When None, the full evidence is used.
options.infer_from: very large source set (many files or long documents) that risks exceeding the model's context window -> set a limit (e.g. 200000)

options.name: parser_options
options.effect: Advanced options passed through to the selected PDF/document parser (e.g. DoclingParser OCR settings). Most use cases do not need this; leave null unless the chosen parser_choice requires specific configuration.
options.infer_from: parser_choice is set to a non-default value AND the parser requires additional configuration

options.name: image_options
options.effect: Options passed to the internal vision/image handler when image files are among the inputs. Key: 'model' (vision model override). When None, the module uses its default vision model.
options.infer_from: input contains standalone image files AND user specifies a preferred vision model

options.name: additional_instructions
options.effect: Free-text instructions appended verbatim as 'ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS:' in both the writer and reviewer prompts for EVERY section (single-call and agentic mode alike). Use for cross-cutting rules that apply report-wide, not per-section (tone, forbidden topics, formatting constraints e.g. 'no bullet points, prose only') -- per-section guidance belongs in that section's own instructions instead.
options.infer_from: requirements mention a report-wide style/tone/format rule, a compliance constraint, or a forbidden-topics list -> set it; section-specific guidance -> put it in the section's instructions field instead

MultiSourceReportGenerator.note: End-to-end report synthesis module: parses/transcribes/extracts every source file itself and writes the full report. Do NOT add parsers, Transcriber, or VisionExtractor as separate steps. Provide input_paths + sections (each with title, instructions, optional id and depends_on). Sections with depends_on are written after their dependencies in agentic mode, receiving finalized dependency content as context. Use save_report_config/load_report_config to persist and reuse use-case configurations. Install multi-source-report-generator-agentic for agentic mode; multi-source-report-generator-docx for DOCX export.

VisionPlusParser.returns_note: Image descriptions are inlined into .parsed_markdown at the position the figure occupies. Pages are flattened into one string -- no page-level provenance.

options.name: enable_ocr
options.effect: OCR for scanned / image-based PDFs. Adds significant CPU time.
options.infer_from: inputs are scanned or image-based PDFs

options.name: ocr_engine
options.effect: OCR backend when enable_ocr=True. 'rapidocr' needs no system dependencies; 'tesseract_cli'/'tesseract' require a system Tesseract install; 'easyocr' is GPU-friendly.
options.infer_from: enable_ocr == true AND no system Tesseract available -> 'rapidocr'

options.name: vision_prompt
options.effect: Overrides the built-in instruction sent to the vision model when describing each detected image.
options.infer_from: domain_vocabulary OR specific requirements about how figures should be described

options.name: enable_table_structure
options.effect: Extract table structure via Docling.
options.infer_from: inputs contain tables

options.name: enable_formula_enrichment
options.effect: Detect and render mathematical notation. Adds processing time; disable for documents without formulas.
options.infer_from: input documents contain formulas or scientific notation -> keep True; otherwise False to reduce latency

options.name: num_threads
options.effect: Docling worker threads.
options.infer_from: leave at default unless throughput tuning is requested

options.name: verbose
options.effect: Print per-stage progress to stdout.
options.infer_from: set False for non-interactive or service deployments

DoclingApiClientParser.construct_note: Requires `import os` -- the PoC templates do not import it, add it explicitly. gaik has NO environment fallback: api_base and password are constructor kwargs and DoclingApiClientParser raises ValueError when either is empty. DOCLING_API_BASE / DOCLING_API_PASSWORD is the convention used by toolkit_demo_app and the OpenShift deployment; the bundled example script uses the older API_BASE / PASSWORD names.
DoclingApiClientParser.returns_note: IMPORTANT: the key is 'parsed_markdown', NOT 'text_content' as on the local DoclingParser. Pages are flattened -- no page-level provenance.

options.name: timeout_seconds
options.effect: HTTP timeout for the parse request. Long documents on a busy server can exceed the default.
options.infer_from: inputs are very large documents -> raise above the 1800s default

options.name: healthcheck_timeout_seconds
options.effect: Timeout for the /health probe issued before each parse.
options.infer_from: leave at default unless the service is known to be slow to wake
